entry.title: LoCA: Enabling Multi-Modality in Geospatial Location Encoders
entry.summary:
Location encoders map geographic coordinates to high-dimensional descriptors through contrastive alignment with paired Earth Observation imagery. We prove that this construction is structurally limited: any Lipschitz location encoder produces an output of intrinsic dimension at most 2, regardless of architecture or bandwidth, which forces the contrastive loss to strictly exceed its asymptotic optimum. Empirically, joint training also collapses the encoder's embedding covariance to low rank.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #combinatorics

entry.title: Doom GPU Flame Graphs
entry.summary:
Imagine halving the resource costs of AI and what that could mean for the planet and the industry -- based on extreme estimates such savings could reduce the total US power usage by over 10% by 2030 1 . At Intel we've been creating a new analyzer tool to help reduce AI costs called AI Flame Graphs : a visualization that shows an AI accelerator or GPU hardware profile along with the full software stack, based on my CPU flame graphs . Our first version is available to customers in the Intel Tiber AI Cloud as a preview for the Intel Data Center GPU Max Series (previously called Ponte Vecchio).

entry.title: The lower tail of triangle counts in sparse random graphs. Let $T_n$ be the number of triangles in the Erdős-Rényi random graph $G(n,p)$ with $n^{-1/2}\ll p\ll1$ and fix $η\in(0,1)$.
entry.summary:
Let $T_n$ be the number of triangles in the Erdős-Rényi random graph $G(n,p)$ with $n^{-1/2}\ll p\ll1$ and fix $η\in(0,1)$. We study the large deviation rate of the lower tail event $T_n\leη\mathbb{E}[T_n]$, and the typical structure of $G(n,p)$ conditioned on this event. By earlier work [16,19,21,49], both the rate and the structure are governed by a variational problem over graphons.

Source: arXiv Mathematics (NT, CO, AG, LO, AT, GR) · Tags: #number-theory #combinatorics #probability-stats

entry.title: Beyond city pairs: Higher-order information in urban growth across borders. We apply higher-order information measures to urban growth across borders and spatial units.
entry.summary:
We apply higher-order information measures to urban growth across borders and spatial units. We analyse 8,808 functional urban areas using gridded GDP estimates allocated from national accounts. Negative estimated O-information occurs in 29.93% of cross-border triplets and 2.00% of domestic triplets.

entry.title: Proximity Theorem and FPT Algorithm for Minimum Group-labeled Matroid Bases
entry.summary:
Let $M$ be a matroid, let $\ell:E(M)\to G$ be a labeling of its elements by an abelian group, and let $F\subseteq G$ be finite. A base is $F$-avoiding if the label sum of its elements is not in $F$. We prove that, for arbitrary costs, a min-cost $F$-avoiding base can be obtained from any min-cost base using at most $|F|$ exchanges.

Source: arXiv CS (PL, SE, DB, DC, DS) · Tags: #compilers #distributed-systems #combinatorics #algorithms

entry.title: Expanding gmx_MMPBSA capabilities for end-state binding free energy calculations with GROMACS and AMBER
entry.summary:
gmx_MMPBSA is an end-to-end tool for performing end-state binding free energy calculations. Here, we present advances in the gmx_MMPBSA suite that simplify preparation, expand the calculation options, and improve the analysis of results. The new features include the GBNSR6 and nonlinear PB models, second-order cumulant (C2) entropy estimation, inclusion of explicit structural waters, and multiple alanine/glycine mutations.

entry.title: TranSAGE: Automating Spatial Accelerator Generation for Large-Scale Transformer Models
entry.summary:
Large-scale Transformers have achieved remarkable success across NLP, computer vision, and robotics, but their growing computational and memory demands challenge efficient inference. Spatial accelerators offer advantages in on-chip bandwidth and energy efficiency, yet designing them for large models remains costly and time-consuming. Existing accelerator generators typically focus on single-operation support, overlooking the benefits of multi-operation pipelining, which limits throughput and energy efficiency.

entry.title: Strongly Adaptive Asynchronous Byzantine Agreement with Linear Communication and Almost-Everywhere Termination
entry.summary:
It is well known that Byzantine agreement requires $\Omega(t^2)$ messages against a strongly adaptive adversary that may corrupt $t=\Theta(n)$ parties and suppress a party's undelivered messages upon corruption. We circumvent this lower bound by relaxing termination: for any constant $0<\nu<1$, at least a $(1-\nu)$ fraction of the honest parties terminate, while agreement and validity hold for every honest decision. For every constant corruption gap $\delta>0$ and every $t\leq(1-\delta)n/3$, we construct binary agreement with this guarantee in authenticated asynchronous networks against strongly adaptive corruptions with message takebacks.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #rust #combinatorics

entry.title: Amortized Multi-Verifier Proofs from Reductions of Knowledge
entry.summary:
We study amortization of prover work in the multi-verifier setting, motivated by proof-as-a-service deployments in which a shared prover serves $K$ independent clients holding distinct statements. Each verifier checks only its own statement and proof, with no inter-verifier communication. The challenge is therefore to amortize prover work across many proofs while preserving local verification.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #combinatorics
